questions.question: Where may fork product edits be made, and what must accompany each fork code change?
questions.answer: Fork product edits belong under apps/mobile/**. An unavoidable outside edit requires a stated necessity. Each fork code change must have surrounding Korean [FORK:Fxxx] markers documenting summary, upstream behavior, fork behavior, reason and conditional default conflict decision, plus a docs/ai-rules/FORK_CHANGES.md ledger entry using a sequential, never-reused ID.
questions.expected: Only apps/mobile/** (outside edits need necessity + same markers + ledger); Korean [FORK:Fxxx] start/end markers with 원본/포크/이유/원본 동일 수정 시 fields and a FORK_CHANGES.md ledger entry.

questions.question: The last fork build was 0.1.13.1 and upstream mobile is still 0.1.13. What versionName and versionCode does the next fork build use? What if upstream mobile moved to 0.1.14?
questions.answer: Upstream remains 0.1.13: versionName 0.1.13.2, versionCode 101302. Upstream moves to 0.1.14: counter resets to 1, versionName 0.1.14.1, versionCode 101401.

questions.question: During an upstream sync, which command lists the fork blocks, and with which git operation is upstream brought into main?
questions.answer: List fork blocks with git grep -n "\[FORK:". Bring upstream into clean main with git merge upstream/main or git merge vX.Y.Z; never rebase/reset main onto upstream.
questions.expected: git grep -n "\[FORK:"; git merge upstream/main or a vX.Y.Z tag, never rebase/reset.

questions.question: Upstream changed the release URL constants in MixdogAppUpdater.java, conflicting with F001. Is it acceptable to resolve with git checkout --theirs on that file?
questions.answer: No. Whole-file git checkout --theirs is explicitly prohibited. F001 is fork identity (case d): preserve moveju112/mixdog release URLs and markers even when upstream changes the same lines. Resolve per block, retaining unrelated upstream changes and adopting security fixes before safely reapplying fork intent.
questions.expected: No: whole-file ours/theirs is forbidden and F001 is identity case d, so the fork URLs are kept while other upstream changes are merged per block.
